en: I want to return this shirt because the stitching is loose.
tamil: இந்த சட்டையோட தையல் தளர்வா இருக்கு, அதனால திருப்பிக் கொடுக்கணும்.
context: Telling the shop staff why you are returning a shirt.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Loose' describes bad stitching.
usage: Use it at the customer service desk of a clothes shop.
leelaQ: Have you ever returned something to a shop?
answer: Yes, I once returned a bag because the zip was broken.

en: Can I get a refund, or only an exchange?
tamil: எனக்கு பணம் திரும்ப கிடைக்குமா, இல்ல மாத்திக்க மட்டும்தானா?
context: Asking about the return policy at a store.
explain: 'Or' offers two choices. A refund means getting your money back.
usage: Use it at the billing counter when you want to return an item.
leelaQ: Would you prefer a refund or an exchange?
answer: I would prefer a refund because I do not need another item.

en: I have kept the bill, so you can check the date.
tamil: நான் பில் வச்சிருக்கேன், நீங்க தேதியைப் பாத்துக்கலாம்.
context: Showing the bill while returning a product.
explain: 'Have kept' shows you still hold the bill now. 'So' gives the result.
usage: Use it when a shopkeeper asks for proof of purchase.
leelaQ: Do you keep your shopping bills at home?
answer: Yes, I keep the bills for big things like a phone or a fridge.

en: There is a mistake in this bill, you have charged me twice.
tamil: இந்த பில்ல தப்பு இருக்கு, ரெண்டு தடவை காசு போட்டிருக்கீங்க.
context: Pointing out a double charge at the billing counter.
explain: 'You have charged' tells about a mistake that has just happened.
usage: Use it politely at a billing counter when the total looks wrong.
leelaQ: What do you do when a bill has a mistake?
answer: I show it to the cashier and ask them to check it again.

en: Could you please give me a carry bag?
tamil: எனக்கு ஒரு கேரி பேக் கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking for a bag at a supermarket counter.
explain: 'Could you please' is a very polite way to ask for something.
usage: Use it at a supermarket counter after your items are billed.
leelaQ: What do you carry your groceries in?
answer: I carry them in a cloth bag that I bring from home.

en: Is this the last piece, or do you have more in the store?
tamil: இதுதான் கடைசி பீஸா, இல்ல உள்ள இன்னும் இருக்கா?
context: Asking if more stock is available.
explain: This question asks about stock. 'Or' gives two possible answers.
usage: Use it when you like an item but want a fresh or undamaged one.
leelaQ: Do you check the stock before you go to a shop?
answer: Yes, I sometimes call the shop first to check the stock.

en: The delivery person left my parcel at the wrong house.
tamil: டெலிவரி ஆள் என் பார்சல தப்பான வீட்டுல வச்சுட்டுப் போயிட்டாரு.
context: Complaining to customer care about a misdelivered parcel.
explain: 'Left' is the past form of 'leave'. 'Wrong house' says what went wrong.
usage: Use it when you call the customer care of an online shop.
leelaQ: What would you do if your parcel went to the wrong address?
answer: I would call the delivery person and then the customer care.

en: I am looking for a gift for my sister, can you suggest something?
tamil: நான் என் தங்கச்சிக்கு ஒரு பரிசு தேடுறேன், நீங்க ஏதாவது சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a salesperson for gift ideas.
explain: 'I am looking for' says what you want now. 'Can you suggest' asks for advice.
usage: Use it with a salesperson when you are not sure what to buy.
leelaQ: What gift would you buy for your sister?
answer: I would buy her a nice handbag or a set of bangles.

en: The price on the tag is different from the price on the screen.
tamil: டேக்ல இருக்கிற விலையும் ஸ்கிரீன்ல இருக்கிற விலையும் வேற வேற.
context: Pointing out a price mismatch at the billing counter.
explain: 'Different from' compares two things. It is a polite way to point out a problem.
usage: Use it at a billing counter when the scanned price is higher than the tag.
leelaQ: Do you check the price when the cashier scans an item?
answer: Yes, I always look at the screen to see the right price.

en: Please do not pack it yet, I want to check the expiry date.
tamil: இன்னும் பேக் பண்ணாதீங்க, எக்ஸ்பைரி தேதியைப் பாக்கணும்.
context: Asking a shop assistant to wait before packing.
explain: 'Please do not' is a polite way to stop someone. 'Yet' means not now.
usage: Use it at a grocery or medical shop before you pay.
leelaQ: Do you check the expiry date when you buy food?
answer: Yes, I always check it, especially for milk and biscuits.

en: How much will it cost if I take three of them?
tamil: மூணு வாங்கினா எவ்வளவு ஆகும்?
context: Asking for a bulk price from a seller.
explain: 'If' makes a condition. Use 'will' in the main part to ask about the result.
usage: Use it when you want a better price for buying more than one.
leelaQ: Do you buy things in bulk to save money?
answer: Yes, I buy rice and oil in bulk because it is cheaper.

en: The shop gave me a free gift with my purchase.
tamil: கடையில நான் வாங்குனதுக்கு ஒரு இலவச பரிசு கொடுத்தாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a free gift at a shop.
explain: 'Gave' is the past of 'give'. 'With my purchase' means along with what I bought.
usage: Use it when you share a good shopping experience with friends.
leelaQ: What is the best free gift you ever got?
answer: I once got a steel water bottle with a pack of groceries.

en: I am waiting in the queue at the billing counter.
tamil: நான் பில்லிங் கவுண்டர்ல வரிசையில நிக்கிறேன்.
context: Telling someone on the phone where you are.
explain: 'I am waiting' shows an action happening now. 'Queue' means a line of people.
usage: Use it on a phone call when you are late because of a long line.
leelaQ: Do you hate waiting in long queues?
answer: Yes, I hate it, so I go shopping on weekday mornings.

en: Do you have a bigger size in the same design?
tamil: இதே டிசைன்ல பெரிய சைஸ் இருக்கா?
context: Asking for a larger size in a clothes shop.
explain: 'Bigger' compares two sizes. 'Same design' means the one you like.
usage: Use it in a clothes shop when the size you tried is too small.
leelaQ: What size do you usually wear?
answer: I usually wear medium, but sometimes I need a large.

en: My phone has stopped working, and it is still under warranty.
tamil: என் போன் வேலை செய்யல, இன்னும் வாரண்டி இருக்கு.
context: Telling a service centre about a faulty phone.
explain: 'Has stopped' shows a result now. 'Under warranty' means the company will repair it.
usage: Use it at a service centre when something you bought breaks early.
leelaQ: What do you do when your phone stops working?
answer: I take it to the service centre and show the warranty card.

en: Will you be able to deliver it before Diwali?
tamil: தீபாவளிக்கு முன்னாடி நீங்க டெலிவரி பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a seller about delivery before a festival.
explain: 'Will you be able to' asks politely if something is possible in the future.
usage: Use it when you order something for a festival and need it on time.
leelaQ: What do you buy before Diwali?
answer: I buy new clothes, sweets and some crackers for the children.

en: I tried to apply the coupon, but it was not working.
tamil: நான் கூப்பனைப் போட முயற்சி பண்ணேன், ஆனா அது வேலை செய்யல.
context: Complaining to online customer care about a coupon.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas. 'Was not working' tells about a problem in the past.
usage: Use it in a chat with customer support on a shopping app.
leelaQ: Do you use coupons when you shop online?
answer: Yes, I always look for a coupon before I place an order.

en: This is a bit expensive, can you come down a little?
tamil: இது கொஞ்சம் அதிகமா இருக்கு, கொஞ்சம் குறைக்க முடியுமா?
context: Bargaining politely at a street shop.
explain: 'A bit' makes the complaint softer. 'Come down' means reduce the price.
usage: Use it at a street market when you want to bargain politely.
leelaQ: Are you good at bargaining?
answer: Not really, but I try to ask for a small discount.

en: We always compare prices online before we go to the shop.
tamil: நாங்க கடைக்குப் போறதுக்கு முன்னாடி எப்பவும் ஆன்லைன்ல விலைய ஒப்பிட்டுப் பாப்போம்.
context: Talking about shopping habits with a friend.
explain: 'Always' shows a habit. 'Before we go' links two actions in time.
usage: Use it when you chat with friends about smart shopping.
leelaQ: Do you compare prices before buying?
answer: Yes, I check two or three apps before I buy anything big.

en: The cashier gave me back the wrong change.
tamil: கேஷியர் எனக்கு தப்பான சில்லறை கொடுத்துட்டாரு.
context: Telling a friend about a billing mistake.
explain: 'Gave back' means returned. 'Wrong change' means the money returned was incorrect.
usage: Use it when you tell someone about a mistake at a shop counter.
leelaQ: Do you count your change after paying?
answer: Yes, I always count it before I leave the counter.

en: Is there a return policy if I do not like the product?
tamil: பொருள் பிடிக்கலன்னா திருப்பிக் கொடுக்கற பாலிசி இருக்கா?
context: Asking about returns before buying online.
explain: 'If' starts a condition. 'Return policy' means the rules for sending a product back.
usage: Use it before buying an expensive item from an online shop.
leelaQ: Do you read the return policy before buying?
answer: No, but I will start reading it for big purchases.

en: I got a message that my order has been shipped.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் அனுப்பிட்டாங்கன்னு எனக்கு ஒரு மெசேஜ் வந்துச்சு.
context: Telling a family member about an order update.
explain: 'Has been shipped' is passive. It tells what happened to the order, not who did it.
usage: Use it at home when you share an update about a parcel.
leelaQ: What are you waiting for from an online order?
answer: I am waiting for a pair of shoes that I ordered last week.

en: Please wait, I will check the stock at the back.
tamil: கொஞ்சம் இருங்க, நான் பின்னாடி ஸ்டாக் பாத்துட்டு வரேன்.
context: A shop assistant asking a customer to wait.
explain: 'Please wait' is polite. 'I will check' promises an action in the near future.
usage: Shop staff say this when an item is not on the shelf.
leelaQ: What would you say if a customer asked for something you did not have?
answer: I would say sorry and offer a similar item.

en: We need to buy groceries for the whole month.
tamil: நாங்க முழு மாசத்துக்கும் மளிகை சாமான் வாங்கணும்.
context: Planning the monthly grocery shopping with family.
explain: 'Need to' shows something necessary. 'For the whole month' tells how long it lasts.
usage: Use it at home when you plan a big shopping trip.
leelaQ: How often do you buy groceries?
answer: I buy vegetables every week and other groceries every month.

en: Could you gift wrap this, please?
tamil: இதை கிஃப்ட் ராப் பண்ணி கொடுக்க முடியுமா?
context: Asking a shop to wrap a present.
explain: "Could you" is a polite request. "Gift wrap" means to cover a present with pretty paper.
usage: Use it at a gift or clothes shop before a birthday or function.
leelaQ: Who did you last buy a gift for?
answer: I last bought a gift for my friend on her birthday.
